subject: Day 74: narrate a Golden Gate walk
bodyText:
Today's focus
The easy stretch is a good time for low-stimulation outdoor input. Today's lead is a calm Golden Gate Park stroller loop with running narration to pair words with what Avi sees.

Action items
- Walk a quiet Golden Gate Park stroller loop most days this week and narrate the trees, water, and birds. Daylight outdoor time supports varied sensory input and Anoushka's cardiovascular recovery.
- Continue 400 IU/day vitamin D supplementation for Avi regardless of outdoor exposure, since sunlight alone does not meet the AAP target for breastfed infants. HealthyChildren vitamin D: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx
- Inquire about first-birthday venues if you have not yet; top SF venues book six to nine months out.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Quiet startle to loud park sounds and wet sneezing; both are normal sensory responses, not signs of illness.
- [monitor] Sleep stretches lengthening then shortening day to day; note the trend rather than reacting to any single night.
- [call within 24h] New feeding refusal, or acute fever onset after an outing.
- [call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher under 90 days, blue lips, or labored breathing. Call the pediatrician same-day for fever and call 911 for blue lips!

Enrichment opportunities
- Use the stroller loop as a sensory-outdoor session: vary the route so the light, sound, and scenery change, keeping the overall stimulation low and the pace slow.
- Name whatever Avi looks at, following his gaze, so the word lands on the object he is already attending to. Romeo et al. 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- After the walk, log 60 to 75 minutes of tummy time across short bouts, looking for chest fully off the floor on his forearms; prone strength now precedes rolling and sitting. HealthyChildren tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 84-91 (~3 months): sleep-consolidation window opens; start anchoring a consistent sleep-wake routine.
- Day 112-126 (4-month visit): RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at you, moves, or makes sounds to keep your attention
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Active engagement — baby is now driving the interaction, not just responding.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-to-get-attention/complete

- Pushes up on elbows during tummy time
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Tripod position. Builds toward eventual rolling.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/pushes-up-on-elbows/complete

- Holds a toy when you put it in his hand
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Voluntary grasp emerging. Soon followed by reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-toy-when-placed/complete

- Smiles on his own to get your attention
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Initiates the smile rather than responding to yours — emerging social agency.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/smiles-to-get-attention/complete

- Chuckles (not yet a full laugh)
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Throaty soft laugh sounds. Precedes the full belly laugh by a few weeks.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/chuckles/complete
